items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: George Carpentier, the ex-heavy weight boxing champion, had a bar next door to the Villa d'Este and he came in the club every night... George laughed about it but he never referred to Oscar as a monkey again.

ctx.x: So when we had finished this night when Freddy didn't show up the cashier said that she would pay us and asked each one how much he earned for a night. The three of us that had come over from the States and were considered the stars of the band were getting 150 franks a night (the equivalent of 50 dollars for 7 days work).

The cashier seemed quite surprised that we were not getting more but not as much as we were when we learned that the pianist was getting 165 franks a night. The bass player, guitarist and drummer were getting a little less than Spider, George and myself. We never learned how much Freddy was getting but it must have been a big taste.

The next night when Freddy came to work the owner of the club told him that he was finished but the band could continue. Freddy started pleading with us not to accept the deal and stick to him which meant that we should refuse to work. But we thought that Freddy had not been fair with us by giving the pianist (who was very good in those days but not considered as an outstanding artist) more than we were getting although we had accepted to come over here for fifty dollars a week.
